hook.line: Some things you know for weeks and only really see on one particular afternoon. Tomás, going through Hernando's chess notebook, has just had one of those moments, and Spanish has a verb for it.
hook.es: Hasta ayer no caí en cuenta de que Hernando ya no volvería.
hook.en: It only dawned on me yesterday that Hernando wouldn't be coming back.

examples.es: Hasta ayer no caí en cuenta de que era su cumpleaños.
examples.en: It only dawned on me yesterday that it was her birthday.

examples.es: De pronto caí en la cuenta de mi error.
Vale cayó en cuenta de que había perdido el tiquete.
examples.en: Vale realised she had lost the ticket.

examples.es: ¿Cuándo caíste en cuenta de que el libro estaba listo?
examples.en: When did it hit you that the book was ready? (to a friend)

examples.es: Caímos en cuenta de que faltaba la llave.
examples.en: It dawned on us that the key was missing.

examples.es: Mariana no cayó en cuenta de que era tarde.
examples.en: It didn't occur to Mariana that it was late.

rule:
To say that something suddenly clicked, Spanish uses *caer en cuenta de que…*, literally "to fall into the realisation".

*Caí en cuenta de que era tarde.* It dawned on me that it was late.

The verb *caer* changes like any other: *caí*, *caíste*, *cayó*, *caímos*. After *de que* you say what you realised.

English just says "realise" for both a slow understanding and a sudden one. Spanish keeps *darse cuenta* for the plain, general sense and uses *caer en cuenta* for the moment the penny drops. Many speakers also say *caer en la cuenta*; both are fine.
smallPrint: Teachers call this an idiomatic verb phrase. It is followed by *de que* and a clause, or by *de* and a noun: *caí en cuenta de mi error*.

readAndPick.es: Caí en cuenta de que era tarde.
options: It dawned on me that it was late.
It dawned on her that it was late.
It dawned on us that it was late.

readAndPick.es: Vale cayó en cuenta de que faltaba la llave.
options: I realised the key was missing.
Vale realised the key was missing.
You realised the key was missing.

readAndPick.es: Caímos en cuenta de que el café cerraba hoy.
options: They realised the café closed today.
I realised the café closed today.
We realised the café closed today.

readAndPick.es: ¿Caíste en cuenta de que hoy es lunes?
options: Did it hit you that today is Monday? (to a friend)
Did it hit her that today is Monday?
Did it hit me that today is Monday?

readAndPick.es: De pronto caí en la cuenta de mi error.
options: I made a mistake on purpose.
Suddenly I realised my mistake.
I slowly forgot my mistake.

readAndPick.es: Tomás cayó en cuenta de que Hernando no volvería.
options: Tomás has just spoken to Hernando.
Tomás forgave Hernando.
It dawned on Tomás that Hernando wouldn't return.

readAndPick.es: Los clientes no cayeron en cuenta de que el café cerraba.
options: The customers didn't realise the café was closing.
The customer didn't realise the café was closing.
The customers didn't want the café to close.

readAndPick.es: Tomás caerá en cuenta tarde o temprano.
options: Tomás realised it long ago.
Tomás will realise sooner or later.
Tomás is realising it right now.

readAndPick.es: Caí en cuenta de que tenía hambre.
options: I was hungry all day.
I wanted to eat dinner.
It suddenly hit me that I was hungry.

yourTurn.prompt: Choose *caí* or *cayó*: Vale ___ en cuenta de que era tarde. Type the whole sentence.
yourTurn.answer: Vale cayó en cuenta de que era tarde.
accept: Vale cayó en la cuenta de que era tarde.
yourTurn.why: Vale is one person, not me, so the verb is *cayó*.

yourTurn.prompt: Choose *caí* or *caímos*: Mi hermana y yo ___ en cuenta de que faltaba la llave. Type the whole sentence.
yourTurn.answer: Mi hermana y yo caímos en cuenta de que faltaba la llave.
accept: Mi hermana y yo caímos en la cuenta de que faltaba la llave.
yourTurn.why: My sister and I is "we", so *caímos*.

yourTurn.prompt: It dawned on me that it was late.
yourTurn.answer: Caí en cuenta de que era tarde.
accept: Caí en la cuenta de que era tarde.
yourTurn.why: *Caí en cuenta de que* + what you realised.

yourTurn.prompt: When did it hit you that the book was ready? (to a friend)
yourTurn.answer: ¿Cuándo caíste en cuenta de que el libro estaba listo?
accept: ¿Cuándo caíste en la cuenta de que el libro estaba listo?

yourTurn.answer: De pronto caí en la cuenta de mi error.
accept: De pronto caí en cuenta de mi error.
yourTurn.why: With a noun, use *de* instead of *de que*.

yourTurn.prompt: Make it negative: Tomás cayó en cuenta de que era tarde.
yourTurn.answer: Tomás no cayó en cuenta de que era tarde.
accept: Tomás no cayó en la cuenta de que era tarde.

yourTurn.prompt: Make it about we: Caí en cuenta de que tenía hambre.
yourTurn.answer: Caímos en cuenta de que teníamos hambre.
accept: Caímos en la cuenta de que teníamos hambre.

pitfalls.wrong: Caí cuenta de que era tarde.
pitfalls.right: Caí en cuenta de que era tarde.
pitfalls.why: Almost. The little word *en* is part of the phrase and cannot be dropped.

pitfalls.wrong: Caí en cuenta que era tarde.
pitfalls.right: Caí en cuenta de que era tarde.
pitfalls.why: Almost. After *cuenta* you need *de que*, as with *darse cuenta de que*.

pitfalls.wrong: Me caí en cuenta de que era tarde.
pitfalls.right: Caí en cuenta de que era tarde.
pitfalls.why: Almost. Here *caer* has no *me*: say *caí*, not *me caí* (that means "I fell down").

personal: Think of something you only noticed recently, even something small, and say it: *Hasta ayer no caí en cuenta de que…*.
